core_obligations: For the direction from torsion freeness of M to the local condition, apply that localisation preserves torsion freeness at each maximal ideal (proof lines 4859-4860).

For the converse, suppose an element x of M is annihilated by a nonzero ring element; localise at a maximal ideal containing the annihilator and use the local vanishing criterion to obtain a contradiction (proof lines 4859-4861).
Conclude that M is torsion free exactly when every localisation at a maximal ideal is (proof line 4861).

difficulty_reason: The lemma replaces the global condition of being torsion free over a domain by a local one: a module is torsion free if and only if all of its localisations at maximal ideals are torsion free over the corresponding local rings (statement lines 4850-4855). The author's proof is a hint rather than a full argument (proof lines 4858-4861): it says to use that localisation at a multiplicative set preserves torsion freeness, together with a criterion of the Algebra chapter which states that a module is zero if and only if all its localisations at maximal ideals are zero. A reader has to combine the two: an element of M annihilated by a nonzero ring element survives as such after localising, so torsion freeness of all localisations forces there to be no such element and conversely torsion freeness of M passes to localisations by the preceding statement of the section. The proof is recorded here with its hint intact and no step added to it.
